summary: The note covers the Winchester Mystery House, a property and mansion said since its construction in 1884 to be haunted by ghosts of people killed with Winchester rifles. Its construction, under Sarah Winchester's day-to-day guidance, is said by some accounts to have run around the clock until her death on September 5, 1922. Her biographer disputes that account, saying she routinely dismissed workers for months at a time and that claims of ceaseless work for thirty-eight years contradict this.
one_line: Covers the Winchester Mystery House's reputed hauntings and the disputed claim that its construction never stopped until Sarah Winchester died in 1922.
key_facts: The Winchester Mystery House property and mansion were claimed by many to be haunted since its construction in 1884.
The claimed ghosts were said to be those killed with Winchester rifles.
Under Winchester's day-to-day guidance, the mansion's from-the-ground-up construction proceeded around the clock by some accounts.
By some accounts, construction proceeded without interruption until Sarah Winchester's death on September 5, 1922.
Work immediately ceased at Sarah Winchester's death, according to some accounts.
Sarah Winchester's biographer says she routinely dismissed workers for months at a time.
Sarah Winchester is quoted as saying she dismissed workers 'to take such rest as I might'.
The biographer says claims that work at the ranch was ceaseless for thirty-eight years flies in the face of the evidence.
Today's Mystery House proprietors claim that work at the ranch was ceaseless for thirty-eight years.
The note's account of construction schedules is contested between the biographer and the current proprietors.
